newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TROUBLED PRIVATE BANK TO INCREASE CAPITAL.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TROUBLED PRIVATE BANK TO INCREASE CAPITAL.

text.p: Shareholders of Romanian private bank Dacia Felix SA, which awaits a court ruling on its reorganisation or liquidation, decided on Friday to raise the bank's share capital to 150 billion lei from 45 billion.
A shareholders' meeting in the Transylvanian city of Cluj, where the bank is headquartered, voted to make the increase through a private placement.

Stockholders in Dacia Felix -- once a fast growing bank but struggling with bad debts of some $200 million and a 642.2 billion lei 1995 loss -- also decided to annul a regulation in its statute limiting to 20 percent the stock aquired by a single investor.
"It is the sole way to recover and attract investors," a bank executive said.
Under a recovery programme, submitted to a local court last year, four foreign and local companies offered to inject capital or grant credits to Dacia Felix.
According to the law, the central bank, which happens to be Dacia's main creditor, has to clear all equity offers.
The court in Cluj is expected to call a creditors' meeting and eventually rule on the bank's recovery plan or liquidation.
In the seven years since the collapse of communism in Romania, not a single bank has been declared bankrupt.

Under a 1996 law the central bank was allowed to give credits to Dacia Felix and another troubled private bank Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA to help them redeem small depositors. ($=5,677 lei)
